topic: What interference mitigation strategies are required when combining non-adjacent Inmarsat channels for radar while maintaining network QoS?
consensus_response: When combining non-adjacent Inmarsat channels for radar, interference mitigation is crucial to maintain network Quality of Service (QoS). Inter-channel interference (ICI) and co-channel interference (CCI) arise from overlapping frequency bands, reducing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and degrading performance. To mitigate these effects, consider implementing Rate Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA), which allocates resources efficiently and minimizes interference. Additionally, Interference-Aware Routing can optimize network resource allocation and reduce the impact of interference on QoS. By employing these strategies, radar applications can maintain accurate target detection while ensuring QoS is maintained.
reference_context: Combining non-adjacent Inmarsat channels for radar applications leads to increased effective bandwidth up to 1 MHz, enhancing range resolution but introducing new sources of interference such as ICI and CCI. High fixed latencies on links negatively impact the QoS, which is currently not considered in existing QoS provisioning methods.
